hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with fever (single temp >38.3°C or sustained >38.0°C for 1h) and absolute neutrophil count <500 cells/µL. This is a MEDICAL EMERGENCY — mortality high without immediate antibiotics. Most commonly seen post-chemotherapy. Often no localizing signs of infection because there are no neutrophils to create pus/inflammation. Blood cultures x2, UA + culture, CXR. Calculate MASCC score for risk stratification (low-risk may be outpatient). Treatment: empiric IV antibiotics within 1 HOUR — monotherapy with anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime, meropenem, pip-tazo). Add vancomycin if: hemodynamic instability, suspected catheter infection, skin/soft tissue infection, known MRSA colonization, severe mucositis. If persists >4-7 days → add antifungal coverage. G-CSF may be considered. Admit. Reverse isolation (neutropenic precautions).
